Subject: Compact on‑prem cluster: tiling approach + retention constraints

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're drafting the internal requirements for our compact on‑prem site (single rack, limited power) and I wanted to capture a few open questions so the proposal can be priced correctly: 

- Minimum viable cluster size you recommend for the Redwood runtime when we want predictable latency for 3 concurrent inference services (approx 50 qps combined).
- Strategy for separating GPU and CPU workloads — do you recommend co‑located smaller GPU nodes (tiling) or a dedicated GPU pool? Tradeoffs we should expect.
- Storage retention: we need a formal retention/eviction window for KV caches and any local logs. Our legal team requires 90 days retention for customer logs and purge on request. How does Redwood support that in on‑prem?
- KMS/HSM: can we bring our own key material (AWS CloudHSM) and integrate with the private control plane?

I've attached our initial node inventory (TerraHealth_MVP_nodeplan.xlsx) so you can see the physical constraints. If it's easier to discuss on a short call, we can do Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
James

Hi James — appreciated the nodeplan, that helps. Quick answers up front, then a suggested next step.

Short answers:
- Minimum: for predictable latency at ~50 qps we typically see 3 control nodes + 4 worker tiles (mix of cpu/gpu) as the practical MV cluster in a compact rack. That gives headroom for rolling updates and one‑node failures.
- GPU vs CPU: for low power/rack constrained sites we recommend tiling — i.e., small uniform worker tiles where each tile can be tagged for GPU or CPU tasks and autoscaled independently. This reduces overprovisioning versus a single large GPU pool.
- Retention: Redwood on‑prem exposes a retention policy for local caches/logs via the control plane; we can enforce 90d retention and provide a purge API for subject‑access requests. We will need to map that to your backup/archival policy for longer retention on central storage.
- KMS/HSM: BYOK is supported — we can integrate with your CloudHSM over the private link. Key access is limited to the control plane and the local KMS agent; we will document the exact handshake.

Next step: we've drafted a mutual action plan that includes the tiling template, minimum hardware profiles, and the retention SOW. I'm attaching mutual_action_plan_v2.docx for review — can you confirm availability for a 30‑minute alignment call on Wed 8/5 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 8/6 14:00–14:30 PT?

Regards,
Irene

James — adding some technical detail so your infra team can validate against the spreadsheet. Quoting your note: "single rack, limited power."

Design notes (high level):
- Tiling model: define a tile as a repeatable unit (1x controller buddy + 2–3x worker blades). For your rack constraints we recommend 4 tiles: 2 CPU tiles, 2 GPU tiles (NVIDIA T4 class or equivalent) — this supports 50 qps with safe headroom.
- Node types: 
  * tile-control (2 vCPU reserved, 16GB RAM, small disk) — runs control plane pods and local state manager
  * worker-cpu (8 vCPU, 64GB RAM, NVMe cache 500GB) — inference workers for non‑GPU models
  * worker-gpu (1 x T4, 24 vCPU host, 256GB RAM, NVMe 1TB) — pinned device plugin, low latency PCIe attach
- Storage classes: ephemeral NVMe for KV and model cache (local filesystem + optional LVM slice), and replicated blockstore (NFS/SMB or central SAN) for checkpoints/backups. We prefer local NVMe for model KV to avoid network jitter.
- Retention and purge: control plane enforces a 90d TTL for logs; KV caches use LRU with a TTL overlay for explicit purge on request. We'll expose an endpoint that accepts a request id and a subject (SaaS/tenant id) to delete any persisted items within a 24–72 hour SLA.
- Network + egress: recommend an outbound egress gate (restricted NAT/proxy) with allowlist to Redwood update endpoints and your KMS. We can ship a small egress proxy container that does per‑tenant telemetry obfuscation.

Operational constraints:
- Rolling upgrades in tiling are fast if tiles are independent; ensure your rack power budget supports powering down 1 tile at a time.
- If you want full node evacuation semantics for 1hr retention windows we will need a dedicated staging disk for checkpoint streaming.

I'll be on the Wed 10:00 PT slot if that works.
